title: Saturn Systems — Edge private deploy field notes
body:
Meeting: 2025-11-01 10:30 PT — Initial call + environment discovery
Participants: Avery Chen (RWI), Jamal Ortiz (RWI), Priya Narayanan (RWI), Elliot R. (Saturn Eng), Marta L. (Saturn DevOps), Simone (Saturn SecOps)

Purpose: capture customer constraints + quick wins for their edge/private deployment. Saturn is evaluating a small-footprint on-prem inference node for per-site call-center assistants (70% PII) and strict egress restrictions. They want a canary plan for 7 pilot sites.

High level asks (customer):
- On-prem/private instance that never sends PII offsite.
- Support for a ~13B open model (they mentioned Llama-derivative) quantized to 4-bit for cost and footprint.
- p50 latency < 250ms for short prompts (<= 128 tokens), p95 < 1s.
- ~40 concurrent requests per box sustained, burst to 80 for 30s.
- Audit logs of inference calls, identity via SAML SSO + API keys mapped to operator ids.
- Integrate with their Vault (HashiCorp HSM) for model encryption keys.

Environment constraints (Saturn):
- Air-gapped sites. No outbound to public internet by default; they can open 443 only to specific IPs via a change window.
- Each site hardware: 1x A5000 or equivalent (24GB) + 1x NVME 2TB. Some sites have 48GB A6000.
- Kernel: RHEL 8.8. They run containerd 1.7 and currently CUDA 11.8 drivers.
- Strict firewall managed by central SecOps; changes need change ticket 5 days lead.
- Must use internal KMS (HashiCorp) with HSM-backed key wrapping — no external KMS.

Quick engineering notes / gotchas we flagged:
1) Tokenization mismatch risk: Saturn's UI pre-tokenizes input on the client (JS) and sends token counts separately. If the model/tokenizer choice differs, reported tokens will disagree with server-side accounting. Recommend we ship a small client-side library (or a snippet) that uses the same tokenizer we serve.
2) KV cache warm-up + cold-start latency: with quantized 4-bit weights and single GPU we expect first-request p95 to be higher (1.5–2s) due to model page faults and GPU memory population. Plan for a warm-up job on deploy.
3) NVME layout: model shards + mmap are needed. If they run LVM thin-provisioning we may see IO stalls under load. Ask: can they dedicate a raw partition for model store?
4) Driver/CUDA mismatch: they are on CUDA 11.8; our recommended binary runtime for the model optimizations uses 12.x kernels. If they cannot upgrade, fallback path will be slightly slower kernels and disable some attention kernels. Actions: capture exact driver versions per site.
5) Air-gapped control plane: our Private control plane can run inside their VPC but we need at least bootstrap access to pull images once during setup. We proposed an 'image bundle' tarball they can import.
6) Audit log volume: at 40 concurrency and average 100 tokens per request, expect ~3–4GB/day of JSON audit logs per site — they need retention policy or offload plan.
7) HSM integration: need a KMS adapter that uses the HashiCorp API. Ticket required for an integration adapter (JIRA-12872).
8) Streaming: some of Saturn's UI components expect SSE streaming every 50ms; with their constrained network buffering this caused reordering in our PoC. Recommendation: use chunked streaming with 150–200ms flush intervals and ensure backpressure support in their frontend.

Performance assumptions used for sizing (rough):
- Model: ~13B, 4-bit quant -> ~22–26GB GPU memory req (kv cache at 2.5MB/request)
- With A5000 24GB some sites will be tight; A6000/48GB preferred for stable p95.
- Expected throughput per box at target latency: ~60 tokens/s sustained -> ~40 QPS short prompt equivalent.

Suggested configuration / quick wins:
- Use Redwood Private (on-prem package) shipped as an image bundle. Disable control-plane egress by default; allow control-plane attest during scheduled window.
- Provide a preseeded tokenizer bundle and a small client JS lib (tokenize(), checksum) to align client/server token accounting.
- Opt to run a lightweight companion process to pre-warm KV cache on a rolling basis (cron job using synthetic prompts).
- Start pilots on sites with A6000 first. Provide a performance/acceptance checklist for SecOps change window.

Acceptance criteria for pilot (per site):
- Functional: infer calls succeed for 95% of requests in 1 week; no PII leaves the node (verify via network egress test).
- Perf: p50 < 250ms, p95 < 1s on short prompts (<=128 tokens) for 7-days continuous load test at target concurrency.
- Security: HSM-based key wrapping tested and logs ingested into their ELK stack.

Next steps (owners / dates):
- Capture exact driver/CUDA + containerd versions across 7 pilot sites — Owner: Marta (Saturn) — due 2025-11-05.
- RWI: build image bundle export and packaging plan for air-gapped import (prototype) — Owner: Jamal — due 2025-11-10 (JIRA-12872).
- RWI: produce client tokenizer snippet + README + license blurb — Owner: Avery — due 2025-11-07.
- Sec review: draft list of IPs/URLs that must be allowed during bootstrap — Owner: Priya — due 2025-11-06.
- RWI + Saturn: schedule change window with SecOps for image import and control-plane bootstrap — Owner: Elliot (Saturn) — target 2025-11-17.
- Internal: create a load-test script (locust) with sample prompt set and expected RPS/latency curve — Owner: Solutions QE (name TBD) — due 2025-11-12.

Immediate action items (today):
- I will (Avery) draft the tokenizer snippet and push to GH PR (linked artifact).
- Jamal to start packaging plan for image bundle; need checklist of what to include (containers, model artifacts, manifests, checksums).
- Priya to get list of allowed maintenance windows from Saturn SecOps and confirm change ticket SLA.

Open questions / risks to resolve:
- Can Saturn upgrade drivers to CUDA 12.x on A5000s? If not, what is acceptance of the slower kernel?
- Will SecOps allow scheduled outbound to our bootstrap URL or will they insist on fully offline import? If fully offline, we need to finalize image-bundle transfer procedure and checksum workflows.
- Is the desired model a community Llama-derivative with permissive license? Need to confirm license and export controls.

Notes from call (raw, rough):
- Marta: "we can't have any PII egress, even metadata about prompt length if it's tied to user id" — need to see how audit log pseudonymization works.
- Elliot: cares about per-operator API keys mapped to SAML id.
- Simone: wants to see compliance artifacts (SOC2-ish) around image build process.

Proposed doc links to send to Saturn after this call:
- quickstart: air-gapped private deploy checklist (CONFLUENCE-4443-edge-deploy-plan)
- tokenizer snippet (GH PR link)
- sample acceptance test script (will attach after locust script ready)

Scratch thoughts for packaging list (work in progress):
- container images tarball (registry/sha list + inlined manifests)
- model shard tar (sha256), tokenizer bundle, vocab checksum file
- pre-warm synthetic prompt runner binary + config
- install script that validates GPU/CUDA and warns about driver mismatch
- HSM adapter binary + README for integration with HashiCorp

Bottom line / ask: Saturn is a high-value pilot. We need to prioritize air-gap image-bundle and tokenizer alignment. Short term: get driver versions and secops window. Mid term: prototype image bundle and run canary on 1 A6000 site.

-- end of notes --
